svg.aria-label: How to write ਟ · ਠ · ਡ: 3 letters, ਟ, ਠ, ਡ, one after another
svg.title: Writing ਟ · ਠ · ਡ
svg.desc: 3 letters written one after another: ਟ, ਠ, ਡ (gurmukhi). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGurmukhi-Static.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ਟ: GNPS, Gurmukhi Sikho (GNPS Learning Hub), Alphabet Tracing lesson, ਟ (tainkaa) checkpoints, strokes 1–2 (lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart line 509, commit de1e560; Apache-2.0) <https://github.com/codemanxdev/gnps_learning_hub/blob/de1e56014cb0caf7e56de2320681781cae6a7e41/lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart#L509>; ਠ: GNPS, Gurmukhi Sikho (GNPS Learning Hub), Alphabet Tracing lesson, ਠ (thathaa) checkpoints, strokes 1–2 (lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart line 535, commit de1e560; Apache-2.0) <https://github.com/codemanxdev/gnps_learning_hub/blob/de1e56014cb0caf7e56de2320681781cae6a7e41/lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart#L535>; ਡ: GNPS, Gurmukhi Sikho (GNPS Learning Hub), Alphabet Tracing lesson, ਡ (daddaa) checkpoints, strokes 1–2 (lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart line 564, commit de1e560; Apache-2.0) <https://github.com/codemanxdev/gnps_learning_hub/blob/de1e56014cb0caf7e56de2320681781cae6a7e41/lib/data/lessons/lesson_tracing.dart#L564>. Source notes on variation: ਟ: GNPS's children's Punjabi app (Apache-2.0; developer CodeManX) has a tracing lesson whose checkpoints the developer entered over the Noto Sans Gurmukhi letter, one list per pen-down stroke, and whose trace widget makes the child reach them in order. It writes ਟ in two pen-down strokes: the headline from left to right; then from the top right down the short stem, left and down the left side, and round the base to the bottom right. The headline first is the source's teaching order. Fluent writers are often described as adding the headline last (Alfaazo's general guidance on Gurmukhi; native Devanagari writers do so in HP Labs India's pen data), so the path shows how this lesson teaches the letter, not how every fluent hand writes it. Omniglot (Lake, Salakhutdinov & Tenenbaum, Science 350:1332, 2015; https://github.com/brendenlake/omniglot, MIT licence) holds 20 drawings of ਟ, each by a different non-native copyist; only counts and shares are cited. 90% (18 of 20) draw it in two strokes, the source's count and their most common one. For the first stroke of the body, 65% (13 of 20) start in the same part of the letter as the source and 100% (20 of 20) set off in the same direction, within 45 degrees. Only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from the source; no checkpoint coordinate is copied, and the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gurmukhi outline. Handwriting varies by writer. ਠ: GNPS's children's Punjabi app (Apache-2.0; developer CodeManX) has a tracing lesson whose checkpoints the developer entered over the Noto Sans Gurmukhi letter, one list per pen-down stroke, and whose trace widget makes the child reach them in order. It writes ਠ in two pen-down strokes: the headline from left to right; then from the top of the short stem down, counterclockwise round the bowl and back to where it began. The headline first is the source's teaching order. Fluent writers are often described as adding the headline last (Alfaazo's general guidance on Gurmukhi; native Devanagari writers do so in HP Labs India's pen data), so the path shows how this lesson teaches the letter, not how every fluent hand writes it. Omniglot (Lake, Salakhutdinov & Tenenbaum, Science 350:1332, 2015; https://github.com/brendenlake/omniglot, MIT licence) holds 20 drawings of ਠ, each by a different non-native copyist; only counts and shares are cited. 70% (14 of 20) draw it in two strokes, the source's count and their most common one. For the first stroke of the body, 100% (20 of 20) start in the same part of the letter as the source and 100% (20 of 20) set off in the same direction, within 45 degrees. Only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from the source; no checkpoint coordinate is copied, and the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gurmukhi outline. Handwriting varies by writer. ਡ: GNPS's children's Punjabi app (Apache-2.0; developer CodeManX) has a tracing lesson whose checkpoints the developer entered over the Noto Sans Gurmukhi letter, one list per pen-down stroke, and whose trace widget makes the child reach them in order. It writes ਡ in two pen-down strokes: the headline from left to right; then from the top right down and to the left, clockwise through about two full turns, round the knob and then the lower loop, ending near the bottom right. The headline first is the source's teaching order. Fluent writers are often described as adding the headline last (Alfaazo's general guidance on Gurmukhi; native Devanagari writers do so in HP Labs India's pen data), so the path shows how this lesson teaches the letter, not how every fluent hand writes it. The outline prints the knob as a solid teardrop, so the path loops clockwise inside it. Omniglot (Lake, Salakhutdinov & Tenenbaum, Science 350:1332, 2015; https://github.com/brendenlake/omniglot, MIT licence) holds 20 drawings of ਡ, each by a different non-native copyist; only counts and shares are cited. 80% (16 of 20) draw it in two strokes, the source's count and their most common one. For the first stroke of the body, 70% (14 of 20) start in the same part of the letter as the source and 100% (20 of 20) set off in the same direction, within 45 degrees. Only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from the source; no checkpoint coordinate is copied, and the path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gurmukhi outline. Handwriting varies by writer.
svg.text: How it is written — 3 letters, one after another
Letter 1 of 3 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 4 movements
Letter 2 of 3 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 4 movements
Letter 3 of 3 — 2 strokes · 1 pen lift · 5 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after GNPS, Gurmukhi Sikho (GNPS Learning Hub), Alphabet Tracing lesson, ਟ (tainkaa) checkpoints, strokes 1–2
Letter 2: stroke order after GNPS, Gurmukhi Sikho (GNPS Learning Hub), Alphabet Tracing lesson, ਠ (thathaa) checkpoints, strokes 1–2
Letter 3: stroke order after GNPS, Gurmukhi Sikho (GNPS Learning Hub), Alphabet Tracing lesson, ਡ (daddaa) checkpoints, strokes 1–2
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
